label: Lookbook Runway
description: Campaign-led storefront that opens as a lookbook, not a catalog grid. For fashion and object brands that sell through editorial images first.
signatureMotif: full-bleed campaign frames, sparse type, and shop-the-look after the image
promptHints: Open on a full-bleed campaign still. Product names appear as captions after the image, not as a 4-up card grid above the fold.
PDP is a large photo column plus a slim buy rail — no megastore facet chrome on the first screen.
Keep merchandising editorial: one look, then the SKUs in that look.

layouts: Home is a vertical lookbook: each chapter is a full-width photo (min-h-[70vh]) with a small season label and a Shop the look link that jumps to 2–4 products listed as text + price under the frame.
Collection pages stay image-forward: 2-column alternating tall crops, product title overlaid late or below — never a dense 4-column tile grid with filters as the hero.
Product page: one large photo stack on the left (or full-bleed on mobile), name/price/size/CTA in a narrow right rail. Related items are other looks, not a You may also like card row of 8.
Cart and checkout stay visually quiet so the campaign photography remains the brand, not the chrome.
motifs: White or bone ground, black type, almost no fill buttons until the buy action. Hairlines instead of cards.
Cormorant/Fraunces for look titles; Inter/Manrope for price and size. Tracking wide on season labels.
Photography is styled campaign — models, still life, or runway — not packshots on seamless gray.
antiPatterns: Do not open with megastore-clean: facet sidebar, sort dropdown, and a 4-up product card grid.
Avoid boutique-warm stacked lifestyle cards with rounded peach surfaces and cute badges.
No streetwear-bold dark/neon campaign type or Bebas screaming across the viewport.
Avoid icon-feature rows (Free shipping / Easy returns) as the first content under the hero.
